2-5.title: Yummy Food Power!
2-5.description: Learn how food gives you energy to play and grow!

en.title: Yummy Food Power!
en.welcome: Hi hungry friend! Do you know why we eat food? It's not just because it's yummy! Food gives you POWER to run, jump, and play. Let's learn about food magic!
en.mainContent:
**Food is Fuel:** Your body is like a car. A car needs gas to go. Your body needs **Food** to go! When you eat, the food turns into energy so you can run fast and play hard.

**Rainbow Foods:** The best foods are colorful like a rainbow!
*   **Red:** Apples, strawberries (good for your heart!)
*   **Orange:** Carrots, oranges (good for your eyes!)
*   **Yellow:** Bananas, corn (give you energy!)
*   **Green:** Broccoli, spinach (make you strong!)
*   **Blue/Purple:** Blueberries, grapes (good for your brain!)
Eat the rainbow every day!

**Grow Foods:** Some foods help you grow big and tall! **Protein** foods like chicken, eggs, and beans build your muscles. That's why you need to eat them!

**Energy Foods:** Some foods give you quick energy to play! Bread, rice, and pasta are **Energy Foods**. They help you run and jump!

**Strong Bones:** Milk, cheese, and yogurt have something called **Calcium**. It makes your bones super strong so you don't break!

**Water is Magic:** Your body is mostly water! You need to drink water every day to stay healthy. Water helps everything work right.

**Sometimes Foods:** Candy and cookies are yummy, but they are 'Sometimes Foods.' You can have them sometimes, but not every day. Eat 'Everyday Foods' (fruits, veggies) most of the time!
keyPoints: Food is fuel that gives your body energy
Rainbow foods (colorful fruits and veggies) are the best
Protein foods (meat, eggs, beans) help you grow
Energy foods (bread, rice) help you play
Water is super important for your body
interactionPrompts: What color foods did you eat today?
Can you name a 'Grow Food' (protein)?
Why do you think candy is a 'Sometimes Food'?
en.wisdomMoment: Your body is a gift. When you eat healthy food, you are taking care of your gift!
en.core_metaphor: Food is fuel for your body car
en.cta: At your next meal, count how many rainbow colors you can eat!
en.summary: You learned that food is fuel, rainbow foods are best, protein helps you grow, energy foods help you play, and water is magic!

6-12.title: Nutrition 101: The Science of Eating
6-12.description: Learn about macronutrients, vitamins, and building a balanced plate

en.title: Nutrition 101: The Science of Eating
en.welcome: Food is chemistry! When you eat, your body breaks down molecules to extract energy and building blocks. Let's decode the nutrition label and understand what your body actually needs.
en.mainContent:
**The Three Macronutrients:**

1. **Carbohydrates (Carbs):** Your body's main fuel source. Carbs break down into **Glucose** (sugar) which powers your cells. Types:
   *   **Simple Carbs:** Quick energy (fruit, candy). Fast burn.
   *   **Complex Carbs:** Slow energy (whole grains, oats). Long burn.

2. **Proteins:** The building blocks. Made of **Amino Acids**. Your body uses them to build muscle, skin, hair, and enzymes. Sources: meat, fish, eggs, beans, nuts.

3. **Fats:** Not the enemy! Fats protect your organs, insulate your body, and help absorb vitamins. Types:
   *   **Good Fats:** Avocado, nuts, olive oil.
   *   **Bad Fats:** Trans fats (fried food, processed snacks).

**Micronutrients (Vitamins & Minerals):**
*   **Vitamin C:** Immune system (oranges, peppers).
*   **Vitamin D:** Bone health (sunlight, milk).
*   **Iron:** Carries oxygen in blood (spinach, red meat).
*   **Calcium:** Strong bones and teeth (dairy, broccoli).

**The Balanced Plate:** Imagine your plate divided:
*   **½ Plate:** Fruits and vegetables.
*   **¼ Plate:** Protein (chicken, fish, beans).
*   **¼ Plate:** Whole grains (brown rice, whole wheat bread).

**Hydration:** Your body is 60% water. You lose water through sweat and breathing. Drink 6-8 glasses a day. Dehydration makes you tired and foggy.

**Reading Labels:** The **Nutrition Facts** label tells you:
*   **Serving Size:** How much is one serving.
*   **Calories:** Energy in the food.
*   **Nutrients:** How much protein, fat, carbs, vitamins.
Look for low sugar, high fiber, and real ingredients (not chemicals!).
keyPoints: Three macronutrients: Carbs (fuel), Proteins (building blocks), Fats (protection)
Micronutrients (vitamins/minerals) keep systems running
Balanced Plate: ½ veggies/fruits, ¼ protein, ¼ grains
Hydration is critical (60% of body is water)
Nutrition labels help you make smart choices
interactionPrompts: What did you eat for breakfast? Can you identify the macronutrients?
Why do you think athletes eat a lot of protein?
How much water did you drink today?
en.wisdomMoment: You are what you eat. If you eat junk, you'll feel like junk. If you eat fuel, you'll feel like a rocket.
en.core_metaphor: Food is chemistry; your body is the lab
en.cta: Pick one meal this week and build a 'Balanced Plate.' Take a picture!
en.summary: You've learned about the three macronutrients, micronutrients, the Balanced Plate model, hydration, and how to read nutrition labels.

13-17.title: Nutritional Biochemistry: Metabolism & Performance
13-17.description: Understand how food becomes ATP and optimize for athletic/academic performance

en.title: Nutritional Biochemistry: Metabolism & Performance
en.welcome: Your body is a biochemical factory. Food enters, and through a series of reactions, becomes ATP—the energy currency of life. Let's optimize your input for maximum output.
en.mainContent:
**Cellular Respiration:** Food → ATP (energy)
1.  **Glycolysis:** Glucose breaks down in the cytoplasm → 2 ATP.
2.  **Krebs Cycle:** In the mitochondria → more ATP.
3.  **Electron Transport Chain:** Final stage → 34 ATP.
Total: ~36 ATP per glucose molecule. This is why carbs = quick energy.

**Protein Synthesis:** After you eat protein, your body breaks it into amino acids. Ribosomes use these to build new proteins (muscle, enzymes, hormones). This is why athletes need protein after workouts—to repair muscle tears.

**Fat Metabolism:** Fats are energy-dense (9 cal/gram vs. 4 cal/gram for carbs/protein). Your body stores excess energy as fat (adipose tissue). During low-intensity exercise or fasting, you burn fat for fuel.

**Glycemic Index (GI):** Measures how fast a food spikes blood sugar.
*   **High GI:** White bread, candy (fast spike, fast crash).
*   **Low GI:** Oats, beans (slow rise, sustained energy).
For focus (studying), eat low-GI foods. For quick energy (sports), eat high-GI.

**Nutrient Timing:** 
*   **Pre-Workout:** Carbs for energy (banana, oatmeal).
*   **Post-Workout:** Protein + Carbs for recovery (chicken + rice).
*   **Before Bed:** Casein protein (slow-digesting) to feed muscles overnight.

**Supplements:** 
*   **Creatine:** Increases ATP production (strength).
*   **Caffeine:** Blocks adenosine (alertness).
*   **Omega-3:** Reduces inflammation (recovery).
Food first, supplements second.

**Eating Disorders:** Anorexia, bulimia, and binge eating are serious mental health issues, not 'diet problems.' If you or a friend struggle with food, talk to an adult. Your body deserves fuel, not punishment.
keyPoints: Cellular Respiration converts food to ATP (energy currency)
Protein Synthesis rebuilds muscle; timing matters
Glycemic Index affects energy stability (low GI for focus)
Nutrient Timing optimizes performance (pre/post workout)
Eating Disorders are mental health issues requiring help
interactionPrompts: What did you eat before your last test? Was it high or low GI?
Why do bodybuilders drink protein shakes right after lifting?
Do you know someone struggling with food? How can you help?
en.wisdomMoment: Food is not the enemy. Food is information. It tells your cells how to behave. Send good messages.
en.core_metaphor: Your body is a biochemical factory
en.cta: Track your meals for one day. Note your energy levels 1 hour after eating. See the pattern?
en.summary: You've explored Cellular Respiration, Protein Synthesis, Fat Metabolism, Glycemic Index, Nutrient Timing, Supplements, and Eating Disorders.

18-35.title: Functional Nutrition: Biohacking Your Diet
18-35.description: Optimize nutrition for energy, focus, longevity, and body composition

en.title: Functional Nutrition: Biohacking Your Diet
en.welcome: Nutrition is not one-size-fits-all. Your genetics, microbiome, and goals determine your optimal diet. Let's personalize your fuel.
en.mainContent:
**Macros for Goals:**
*   **Fat Loss:** High protein (1g/lb bodyweight), moderate fat, low carb. Protein preserves muscle in a deficit.
*   **Muscle Gain:** High protein, high carb (for energy), moderate fat. Caloric surplus.
*   **Endurance:** High carb (60-70%), moderate protein, low fat. Glycogen stores.
*   **Ketosis:** High fat (70%), moderate protein, very low carb (<20g). Body burns fat for fuel.

**Intermittent Fasting (IF):** Eating windows (e.g., 16:8 = 16 hours fasting, 8 hours eating). Benefits: autophagy (cellular cleanup), insulin sensitivity, fat loss. Not for everyone (women, athletes may need more frequent meals).

**Gut Microbiome:** Your gut has trillions of bacteria. They affect mood, immunity, and weight. Feed them fiber (prebiotics) and fermented foods (probiotics: yogurt, kimchi, sauerkraut).

**Anti-Inflammatory Diet:** Chronic inflammation ages you and causes disease. Reduce: sugar, seed oils, processed food. Increase: omega-3s (fish), turmeric, greens.

**Nootropics (Brain Food):**
*   **Caffeine + L-Theanine:** Focus without jitters (green tea).
*   **Omega-3 (DHA):** Brain structure (fish oil).
*   **Blueberries:** Antioxidants (protect neurons).
*   **Dark Chocolate:** Flavonoids (blood flow to brain).

**Alcohol:** Ethanol is a toxin. Your liver prioritizes metabolizing it over everything else. It disrupts sleep, dehydrates you, and adds empty calories. If you drink, limit to 1-2 drinks and hydrate.

**The 80/20 Rule:** Eat 'clean' 80% of the time. Enjoy life 20% of the time. Perfection is the enemy of consistency.
keyPoints: Macros should match your goals (fat loss, muscle gain, endurance)
Intermittent Fasting activates autophagy and fat burning
Gut Microbiome health affects mood, immunity, and weight
Anti-Inflammatory Diet slows aging and disease
The 80/20 Rule balances health and enjoyment
interactionPrompts: What is your primary goal right now (fat loss, muscle, energy)?
Have you tried Intermittent Fasting? How did it feel?
What is one inflammatory food you could cut out?
en.wisdomMoment: Discipline is choosing between what you want now and what you want most. Your future self is watching your choices today.
en.core_metaphor: Your diet is your code; debug for optimal performance
en.cta: Calculate your macros for your goal using an online calculator. Track for one week.
en.summary: You've explored goal-based macros, Intermittent Fasting, Gut Microbiome, Anti-Inflammatory eating, Nootropics, Alcohol effects, and the 80/20 Rule.

36-60.title: Nutrition for Longevity: Eating for Healthspan
36-60.description: Optimize diet to slow aging, prevent disease, and maintain vitality

en.title: Nutrition for Longevity: Eating for Healthspan
en.welcome: In midlife, nutrition shifts from performance to preservation. The goal is not just to live longer, but to live better—to extend healthspan, not just lifespan.
en.mainContent:
**Caloric Restriction (CR):** Eating 20-30% fewer calories extends lifespan in every organism tested. It activates longevity genes (Sirtuins) and reduces oxidative stress. You don't have to starve; intermittent fasting mimics CR benefits.

**Protein for Muscle Preservation:** After 40, you lose 1% of muscle mass per year (sarcopenia). High protein (1.2-1.6g/kg) + resistance training preserves muscle. Muscle = metabolic health = longevity.

**Anti-Aging Foods:**
*   **Polyphenols:** Berries, dark chocolate, red wine (resveratrol).
*   **Omega-3s:** Salmon, walnuts (reduce inflammation).
*   **Cruciferous Veggies:** Broccoli, kale (sulforaphane activates detox pathways).
*   **Green Tea:** EGCG (antioxidant, fat burner).

**Glycation & AGEs:** High blood sugar causes proteins to 'glycate' (stick together), forming AGEs (Advanced Glycation End Products). AGEs age your skin, arteries, and organs. Reduce sugar and fried foods.

**Bone Health:** Osteoporosis risk increases with age. Calcium + Vitamin D + Vitamin K2 (directs calcium to bones, not arteries). Weight-bearing exercise stimulates bone growth.

**Hormone Optimization:** Nutrition affects hormones:
*   **Testosterone:** Healthy fats, zinc (oysters, pumpkin seeds).
*   **Estrogen Balance:** Fiber, cruciferous veggies (detox excess estrogen).
*   **Insulin Sensitivity:** Low-carb, high-fiber.

**Mindful Eating:** Slow down. Chew thoroughly. Eat without screens. This improves digestion and prevents overeating. Your body needs 20 minutes to signal fullness.
keyPoints: Caloric Restriction activates longevity genes (Sirtuins)
High Protein preserves muscle mass (sarcopenia prevention)
Anti-Aging Foods (polyphenols, omega-3s) reduce oxidative stress
Glycation (AGEs) accelerates aging; reduce sugar
Mindful Eating improves digestion and satiety
interactionPrompts: Could you realistically eat 20% less? What would you cut?
How much protein are you eating daily? (Calculate it!)
Do you eat while distracted (TV, phone)?
en.wisdomMoment: You can't out-exercise a bad diet. And you can't out-supplement poor food choices. Real food is the foundation.
en.cta: Eat one meal this week in silence, slowly, without distractions. Notice how you feel.
en.summary: You've explored Caloric Restriction, Protein for muscle, Anti-Aging Foods, Glycation/AGEs, Bone Health, Hormone Optimization, and Mindful Eating.

61-102.title: Nourishment as Ritual: Food & Gratitude
61-102.description: Finding joy, connection, and meaning in the act of eating

en.title: Nourishment as Ritual: Food & Gratitude
en.welcome: Food is not just fuel; it is memory, culture, and love. In elderhood, every meal is a sacrament. Let's honor the ritual.
en.mainContent:
**Food as Memory:** The smell of your grandmother's soup. The taste of your mother's pie. Food is a time machine. It carries the past into the present. Cooking and eating these foods is an act of remembrance and reverence.

**The Communion of Eating Together:** Loneliness is as deadly as smoking. Shared meals create connection. The act of breaking bread together is ancient and sacred. Prioritize eating with others, not alone in front of a screen.

**Gratitude Before Eating:** Before you eat, pause. Say grace, or simply think: 'Thank you to the earth, the farmer, the cook.' Gratitude transforms eating from consumption to communion.

**Appetite as Wisdom:** Your body knows what it needs. If you crave salt, you might need minerals. If you crave sweets, you might need energy or comfort. Listen to your body's whispers, not the shouts of habit.

**Simplicity:** You don't need complex meals. A bowl of soup, a piece of fruit, a slice of bread. Simple food, eaten slowly, is enough. Complexity is for the young. Simplicity is for the wise.

**Fasting as Spiritual Practice:** Not eating can be as nourishing as eating. Fasting (skipping a meal, or a day) clears the mind and rests the body. Many spiritual traditions use fasting to connect with the divine.

**The Final Feast:** One day, you will eat your last meal. You don't know when. So treat every meal as if it might be. Savor it. Share it. Give thanks for it.
keyPoints: Food is Memory; it connects us to the past
Shared Meals combat loneliness and build connection
Gratitude transforms eating into a sacred act
Appetite is Wisdom; listen to your body
Simplicity in food reflects simplicity in life
interactionPrompts: What food reminds you most of your childhood?
When was the last time you ate a meal with full attention (no distractions)?
What would you want your 'last meal' to be?
en.wisdomMoment: Bread for myself is a material question. Bread for my neighbor is a spiritual question. (Nikolai Berdyaev). Feeding others is an act of love.
en.cta: Cook a meal from your childhood. Share it with someone you love. Tell them the story of the recipe.
en.summary: You've explored Food as Memory, Communion of Shared Meals, Gratitude, Appetite as Wisdom, Simplicity, Fasting as Spiritual Practice, and the Final Feast.
